description: The negative half of resolving a dotted name against a source tree. Matching a name by suffix is what makes `include("plane.app.urls")` reach a module under `apps/api/`, and it is exactly as capable of reaching the wrong one: a suffix two modules end with says nothing about which the loader finds, and the file that settles it is a deployment's sys.path rather than any source in the repository. AMBIGUITY RESOLVES TO NOTHING, in both directions. `billing.urls` names two URLconfs, so neither takes the `pay/` prefix and both keep the route their own file writes. `jobs.views` names two modules, so `path("run/", job_views.execute)` reaches no handler -- and one of the two `execute` functions concatenates a query parameter into a shell command. Nothing is reported: the engine states in its surface that one function reads caller-supplied input and no entry point reaches it, which is an honest gap rather than a clean bill of health. There are no expectations because a phantom route is worse than a missing one -- an invented entry point sends a maintainer to an address that does not exist, and everything the report says about it is unfalsifiable. If either resolver ever picks one of two candidates, the command injection at `alpha/jobs/views.py` becomes reportable at `/run/` and this corpus fails with a FALSE POSITIVE.
